predecessors.name: Aquitaine
predecessors.text: Gascony, in personal union with Aquitaine 'from 660 to 769' (Duchy of Gascony page)

successors.name: Duchy of Aquitaine
successors.text: Gascony, joined to Aquitaine when Gui-Geoffrey (William VIII), Duke of Gascony from 1052, became Duke of Aquitaine in 1058

ledger.x: 768: the Gascon line begins after the Carolingian takeover of Vasconia.
783: Gascony north of the Pyrenees passes to the Carolingian sub-kingdom.
793: the east edge leaves the shape (bridging a silence).
806: the Franks take Navarre under their protection.
818: the revolt ends with its leader's death.
864: Gascony is effectively independent under Sans III Sancion.
1052: Gui-Geoffrey of Poitiers becomes Duke of Gascony.
1058: Gui-Geoffrey becomes Duke of Aquitaine and Gascony joins the Duchy of Aquitaine.
1058: the Gascon duchy merges into the Duchy of Aquitaine under William VIII; the land passes to the Duchy of Aquitaine's colour (the title survives to 1453 on the Duchy of Gascony page).

wars.name: Battle of Roncevaux Pass (778)
wars.outcome: Basque ambush of Charlemagne's rearguard on 15 August 778 ('led by Roland was attacked by the Basque tribes'); Pamplona's walls were destroyed in the retreat; no change of border.

wars.name: Gascon revolt of 816-818
wars.outcome: Louis the Pious deposed Seguin of Bordeaux (816), a revolt led by García Jiménez followed, and García was killed in 818.

wars.name: Battle of Roncevaux Pass (824)
wars.outcome: 'the second Battle of Roncevaux took place', Frankish counts Eblo and Aznar Galindo captured; the Pamplonese are 'definitively' detached from the duchy and Íñigo Arista is elected king of Pamplona.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey draws any Gascon frontier in the pages opened; the page describes the duchy only as 'between the Garonne and the Adour'.
